purpose: Follow-up research while tracing the audio timing failure; these sources support clock separation, not a claim that a particular release curve is an industry standard.

sources.observation: get_ticks_msec is monotonic and suited to elapsed intervals; verified against this project's actual Godot 4.7.2 behavior.
Game time scale affects process timing; mixing it with a real-time deadline creates inconsistent envelope behavior.
Unity exposes an unscaled real-time update mode for an AudioMixer.
Unreal distinguishes audio scheduling from game-thread frame timing; this project still updates parameters on its main thread and does not claim sample-accurate scheduling.
Audio processing consumes volume and playback parameters independently of game-frame scheduling.

genre_images: design/08-lighting/READABILITY_REFERENCES.md keeps five previously viewed side-view action/exploration games from different development teams. Their images are visual reference, not evidence of how their audio engines work.
decision: Keep existing event depths, hold settings and priority rules. Give hold and release one monotonic clock. Define a finite linear recovery in decibels over the configured release duration; new quiet voices sample that same envelope. This curve is a project decision and must still be auditioned.
